issues.failure_explanation: The expression $tf(x)+(1-t)g(x)$ depends on the chosen real representatives of the two elements of $\mathbb T$; changing one representative by an integer changes the result by generally nonintegral $t$. Equality of winding numbers does not make this pointwise convex combination well defined. Checking only the endpoint values on selected loops also cannot establish a globally defined continuous map on $G$. The converse implication therefore lacks a valid construction of the homotopy.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply a nontrivial global lifting argument, for example by proving that the circle-valued quotient $f-g$ has a continuous real lift when all relevant winding numbers vanish, and use that lift to construct the homotopy.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed classification of homotopy classes by the full winding vector is not proved, so later interpretations of degree vectors as complete homotopy invariants are unsupported.
issues.title: Convex combinations of circle-valued maps are not well defined
issues.why_classification: The theorem may remain true, but replacing the invalid interpolation requires a contained substantive topological argument rather than a routine algebraic correction.

issues.failure_explanation: Both the boundary conditions and all winding numbers are invariant under replacing a harmonic map $f$ by $f+c$ for an arbitrary constant $c\in\mathbb T$. Thus every solution produces an entire circle of distinct solutions. The construction silently removes this symmetry by imposing the additional normalization $f(v_1^0)=0$, but that normalization is absent from the theorem.

failure_location.quote: There is a unique HM $f: G\to\T$ satisfying \eqref{bc-hm} and \eqref{homotopy-c}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add an absolute normalization such as $f(v_1)=0$, or state uniqueness only modulo additive constants in $\mathbb T$.
issues.overall_effect: The uniqueness part of the main theorem and the corresponding uniqueness claims in the introduction and discussion are false as stated.
issues.title: Uniqueness ignores the additive circle symmetry
issues.why_classification: A standard local normalization removes the symmetry without changing the construction, existence result, degree regime, or harmonic-extension method.

diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Thus, $\mathbf{f}^\ast|_{V_m^k}$ is $\Gamma^k_m$-harmonic and
it remains to check that $\mathbf{f}^\ast|_{\tilde V_m}$ satisfies the 
discrete Laplace equation at $z_{\pm}^k$.

issues.failure_explanation: The affine constraint ties the variations of $f(z_-^k)$ and $f(z_+^k)$ together. Stationarity therefore gives only a combined Kirchhoff condition—the sum of the two first variations—not the separate discrete Laplace equations at both cut copies required by the earlier definition of $\Gamma_m$-harmonicity. The later theorem itself recognizes that harmonicity at these points remains to be checked after gluing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict item 1 to unconstrained interior vertices and state the combined stationarity condition at the cut pair; harmonicity at the identified vertex must then be established after gluing.
issues.overall_effect: Item 1 of the lemma is false under the paper's stated definition, although the minimization and compatibility parts may still be usable away from the cut vertices.
issues.title: The minimizer need not be harmonic at the two constrained cut vertices
issues.why_classification: This is a local correction to the harmonicity statement and does not require changing the minimizer or the subsequent separate gluing argument.

issues.failure_explanation: The vertices $v_1^k,v_2^k,v_3^k$ have prescribed Dirichlet values and are not varied in the minimization. Consequently no Euler–Lagrange equation is obtained there, and the paper's own definition of discrete harmonicity excludes $V_0$. The proof only addresses the glued cut vertices and gives no reason for the Laplacian to vanish at the lifted boundary vertices.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace $\forall x\in\tilde V_m$ by quantification over the interior vertices of the covering graph, excluding all lifted copies of $V_0$.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem overstates the harmonicity domain; its displayed conclusion is false for general boundary data.
issues.title: Global discrete harmonicity is incorrectly asserted at prescribed boundary vertices
issues.why_classification: The necessary repair is a local restriction consistent with the intended Dirichlet problem and preserves the interior harmonicity guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: The left-hand energy sums unsquared geodesic distances, whereas the real energy sums squared differences. Even when each edge admits a shortest real lift, these quantities are not equal. The quadratic minimizer constructed earlier therefore is not shown to minimize the energy actually defined in this section, and compatibility of the quadratic forms does not imply the asserted monotonicity for this unsquared functional.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define the circle energy using $d_\mathbb{T}(f(x),f(y))^2$ and adjust the short-edge condition to the injectivity radius for the normalization $\mathbb T=\mathbb R/\mathbb Z$; then justify compatibility using coherent local lifts.
issues.overall_effect: The variational interpretation, the asserted energy equality, monotonicity, and the claimed derivation of the main harmonic-map guarantee from the real quadratic minimizer all fail for the stated functional.
issues.title: The circle energy uses distance rather than squared distance
issues.why_classification: The intended quadratic energy is clear and can be restored by a short local correction plus the corresponding normalization adjustment, without changing the constructed map or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The identification shifts the sheet by the enumeration index $\ell(w)$ rather than by the desired winding number $\rho_{\ell(w)}$. Thus the resulting covering has fixed monodromy determined by the loop's index and generally does not encode the prescribed degree vector. The later jump condition and the appendix use the winding number instead, so they are incompatible with the stated construction.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the shift $k+\ell(w)$ by $k+\rho_{\ell(w)}$ and consistently use the two itineraries of the selected cut point.
issues.overall_effect: The higher-order covering algorithm does not in general produce a map with the requested winding data, leaving the arbitrary-degree part of the main theorem unsupported as written.
issues.title: Higher-order sheet identifications use the loop index instead of its prescribed winding
issues.why_classification: The source itself supplies the consistent correction in the jump conditions and appendix, and the correction is local without altering the architecture.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where $(c^m_{ij})$ is a positive definite $m\times m$ matrix.

issues.failure_explanation: The displayed sum is indexed only from $1$ to the number $N$ of contractions although its argument is a function on the generally much larger set $V_m$, while the coefficient matrix is simultaneously declared to be $m\times m$. Moreover, positive definiteness of a coefficient matrix does not imply that the individual conductances in the sum are nonnegative; negative off-diagonal entries can make the displayed weighted-difference form nonpositive. Hence the energies and associated graphs used by the proof are not well defined under the stated assumptions.

failure_location.quote:
There is a HM $f\colon K\to\mathbb{T}$ satisfying 
  \eqref{eq:winding_vec_general} and \eqref{pcf-bc-hm}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define coefficients for every pair in $V_m$, require symmetric nonnegative conductances with a connected conductance graph, and formulate the usual positive-semidefinite Dirichlet form together with the stated compatibility and self-similarity conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The minimization, graph approximation, harmonic extension, and existence proof for the general p.c.f. theorem lack a valid common energy structure.
issues.title: The general harmonic structure is not defined by valid conductance forms
issues.why_classification: Repair requires replacing the malformed assumptions by a coherent resistance-form structure; this is standard but more than a single forced index correction because positivity and connectivity hypotheses must also be supplied.

issues.failure_explanation: Because $\mathcal B_m$ is a basis of the cycle space, the cycle $\gamma_0$ is an integer linear combination of its basis cycles. Winding number is additive on cycles, so its winding $\rho_0$ is forced to be the same linear combination of $\rho_1,\ldots,\rho_{n_m}$. The theorem imposes the basis windings and the boundary-loop winding without any compatibility condition; inconsistent choices admit no continuous map, let alone a harmonic one. The notation $\omega_p$ also leaves the relevant loop unidentified.

failure_location.quote:
There is a HM $f\colon K\to\mathbb{T}$ satisfying 
  \eqref{eq:winding_vec_general} and \eqref{pcf-bc-hm}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Identify $p$ with the chosen oriented cycle $\gamma_0$, express $[\gamma_0]$ in the chosen cycle basis, and require $\rho_0$ to equal the resulting integer linear combination of the prescribed $\rho_i$.
issues.overall_effect: The existence theorem is false for admissible-looking but incompatible winding and boundary data.
issues.title: The prescribed boundary winding need not be compatible with the cycle-basis windings
issues.why_classification: Adding the necessary linear compatibility condition is a local restriction on the data and preserves the same existence construction for compatible inputs.
